title: Lost Projects
content:
I downloaded the new update and when I tried to open my projects I just saved less than an hour ago, they all disappeared. I'm very frustrated and annoyed.


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, did you save your projects within the CLO assets folders? If yes, they unfortuentely cannot be recovered. If this is not the case, the link in the library might be gone, but the files should still be on your computer.
Reply 1: omg this just happened to me you're sayign everything i worked for for the last few months is gone???

title: Crash When Exporting Pattern as PDF in Print Layout
content:
I’m currently using Clo3D version 2024.2.328. Whenever I switch to the Print Layout mode and attempt to take a snapshot of my pattern to save as a PDF, the software crashes. This happens consistently across all my projects, regardless of their complexity or size.

It’s worth noting that this feature was functioning properly before the most recent minor update. The issue seems to have started immediately after that update.

Can I put go back to the pervious working version?


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, you can get previous patches here: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/2ee39b955f0245979c4195c4bc67add6 you please open a ticket for tech support here: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/2ee39b955f0245979c4195c4bc67add6 the issue, and include either a dxdiag.txt (https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/2ee39b955f0245979c4195c4bc67add6 if on Windows or an About This Mac window screenshot if on Mac, so they can investigate the problem? They can also check the crashlog of your account. Thank you!
content_description: This webpage aims to provide guidance on resolving the Clo3D 2024.2.328 crash issue when taking snapshots in Print Layout mode and options for reverting to a previous stable version.

title: Unable to Export Button as OBJ【CLO】【MD-OK】
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/cf27eb8453e143ddaf1170df46674423/images/79b350c793b34cec8f392df90b972dc8%E3%82%B9%E3%82%AF%E3%83%AA%E3%83%BC%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B7%E3%83%A7%E3%83%83%E3%83%88%202025-03-11%20111114.png)

When I import a button exported from CLO into Blender, it only appears as vertices.

However, when I try the same process in MD, the button exports as an OBJ without any issues.

Is anyone else experiencing problems exporting buttons as OBJ from CLO?

**Versions:**

  * **CLO:** 2024.2.296

  * **MD:** 2024.2.177




* * *

CLOからエクスポートした釦をBlenderにインポートすると、頂点のみが表示されてしまいます。

しかし、同じ手順をMDで試すと、釦は問題なくOBJとしてエクスポートされました。

CLOから釦をOBJでエクスポートできていますか？

**バージョン:**

  * **CLO:** 2024.2.296

  * **MD:** 2024.2.177





### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: こんにちは！コミュニティチャンネルをご利用いただき、ありがとうございます！さて、ご質問の件についてご回答いたします。CLOからボタンをOBJ形式でエクスポートすることが可能です。必要に応じて、詳細な手順をご案内できますので、お気軽にお知らせください！また、不具合が発生したファイルをご共有いただければ、開発チームにて詳細を確認いたします。引き続きよろしくお願いいたします。 😊
Reply 1: お返事ありがとうございます。もう一度、2.328個人版、2.296企業版で試しましたが出来ませんでした。データを送るので、対応を教えていただけると幸いです！🙏🏻

title: 3D to Reality: Ataa’s Butterfly Dress for ETTOI
content:
## _Ataa, winner of the Spring 2024 CONNECT x ETTOI contest, shares her design journey, while ETTOI discusses its sustainability and the collaboration’s impact._

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/986a6695219e4bef93faf8de72a019a4main.png)

* * *

# **Interview with**

# **Ataa | CONNECT Creator, 3D Fashion Artist**  
**ETTOI | Premium Children’s Wear Brand**

#   
**Ataa’s Journey: From Passion to Winning Design**

Growing up in a tailor family in Indonesia, Ataa was immersed in craftsmanship from an early age. Her passion led her to study fashion design in India, gaining hands-on experience in block printing and design.

Now a 3D Fashion Artist at a Korean factory, she creates for brands like Old Navy, GAP, and Target. Discovering CLO was a game-changer, allowing her to design without fabric waste and bring ideas to life in motion. This opened new possibilities to experiment with visually striking yet practical designs.

# **The Inspiration Behind the Butterfly Dress**

For the contest, Ataa wanted to create**** a dreamlike, joyful piece for children. She started with color—yellow, which she associates with happiness and energy. “It’s a color that instantly feels cheerful, and I knew it would look beautiful on kids,” she says.

Her key inspiration came from childhood imagination. **“Many little girls dream of flying like butterflies or fairies,”** Ataa notes. She recalled her young niece, who loved wearing a butterfly-wing costume with elastic straps. Inspired by this, Ataa designed a dress that would incorporate**butterfly wings** , making it both whimsical and wearable.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/fa3d947947f440df94600edb9a663914Reference%20board.png)

In CLO, she built the base silhouette first, ensuring comfort and movement for children. Then, she added the butterfly wings—her central design element. “At first, it looked too plain, so I introduced soft ruffles that wouldn’t overpower the wings but would enhance the elegance,” she explains. After refining the details, she posed the garment in CLO, added colors, and created a final rendered scene to showcase the dress in a natural setting.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/da5dc6f80b184ff6815930285c865893ataa_1.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/c52b8e698ac64ea7ad4ce8914dfd54e2ataa_2.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/383f405b625749cea18264b86399561aButterfly.png)

When she found out she won the contest, Ataa was thrilled. “It felt like a major milestone in my career,” she shares. Receiving the physical version of her design was even more surreal. “It looked exactly like my 3D version—I couldn’t believe it!”

* * *

# **ETTOI’s Perspective: Bridging Digital and Physical Fashion**

For ETTOI, the collaboration was a chance to explore sustainability and innovation in children’s fashion. “By utilizing CLO’s 3D technology, we could minimize material waste and unnecessary sampling,” the ETTOI team explains. The contest also allowed them to connect with talented designers like Ataa, **who brought fresh perspectives to the brand**.

One of the key reasons ETTOI selected Ataa’s design was **its environmental storytelling**. The dress features an endangered butterfly motif, aligning with ETTOI’s commitment to nature-inspired, sustainable fashion. “The use of a butterfly, especially one that symbolizes environmental awareness, resonated deeply with our values,” the team notes.

# **Turning a Digital Design into Reality**

Bringing the butterfly dress to life came with its challenges. The wing details and hem ruffles required precise adjustments to maintain their intended structure. “We worked closely with our pattern team to refine the butterfly shape, ensuring the shoulder frills looked natural and retained their delicate charm,” ETTOI shares.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/45484264ea5346d4bf780c74e43244e0detail.png)

Another challenge was color accuracy. The team carefully selected a shade of yellow that not only matched the CONNECT design but also looked vibrant and lively on fabric. “The final result captured the essence of Ataa’s original vision while making it even more radiant when worn by a child,” they explain.

When ETTOI first saw the final product, they were impressed. “It had a fresh and imaginative feel—perfect for Spring/Summer. The bright yellow butterflies symbolized the endangered **southern yellow butterfly** , native to Korea, adding depth to the design.” Internally, the design received high praise, and during customer voting, it stood out as a favorite.

# **The Future of Fashion: Digital Meets Physical**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/86cdeacc5b094c3cb45aade45e876c1625SS%EB%A1%9C%EC%97%90%EB%93%9C%EB%A0%88%EC%8A%A4_%EC%9D%B8%EC%8A%A4%ED%83%80%EA%B7%B8%EB%9E%A8%EB%A6%B4%EC%8A%A4%20%283%29.gif)

This collaboration highlights how **3D fashion technology can bridge digital design and real-world production**. “It’s exciting to see CLO and CONNECT making sustainable fashion more accessible,” ETTOI shares.

For Ataa, this experience was transformative. “It proved that digital fashion isn’t just a concept—it’s the future,” she says. “I hope more designers explore 3D tools like CLO to push their creative limits while contributing to a more sustainable industry.”

ETTOI also sees digital fashion as a long-term strategy. “This contest was just the beginning. We’re excited to continue exploring how CLO and CONNECT can enhance children’s fashion production while improving our global competitiveness,” they conclude.

* * *

Discover the winning design [**here**](https://connect.clo-set.com/contest/46?itemId=dabe809b071743699ea61013d62a6861) and explore [**Ataa’s creator profile**](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/268915/collection/collections) on CONNECT. You can also find the physical garment available for purchase on the [**ETTOI online store**](https://agabangmall.com/goods/goods_view.php?goodsNo=1000038318 ).

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/31ee111a542b4653927c8f1208731e0cThumbnail.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/fc90cfd13aaf4fa3931ad62c810afacbThumbnail.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/37749dc19d574616bd80f78d3284aab5Thumbnail.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/e77f113bf3bf48aea7a4797c4a1c7e9d/images/dd7ba593db734126812526249a1edbadThumbnail.png)
content_description: Explore Ataa's inspiring design journey as the winner of the Spring 2024 CONNECT x ETTOI contest, highlighting the collaboration's innovative approach to sustainability in children's fashion.
